prompt:
Real laparoscopic cholecystectomy footage. The FIRST image is the opening frame and the SECOND image is the closing frame of the same continuous shot, a few seconds apart. Generate only the motion that connects them: the clip must start exactly on the first image and end exactly on the second image.

What is in the scene (taken from the real frames):
A circular laparoscopic view is framed by a black border. A brushed metallic grasper with dark circumferential shaft bands and serrated, fenestrated jaws enters from the right edge, touching the pale yellow-pink connective tissue and engaging a dissected window below the gallbladder. A second metallic grasper tip enters from the lower-left edge, holding the pale yellow-pink fatty tissue at the gallbladder neck. A third thin metallic shaft is barely visible at the top-center edge against the superior gallbladder fat. The gallbladder occupies the upper-left quadrant, showing a bluish-purple wall covered with fine dark red vessels and lobulated yellow-orange fat. The smooth, reddish-brown liver parenchyma fills the right half of the frame, displaying small pale yellowish-white patches on its glistening surface. Below the dissected tissue bridge, a dark brown fluid pool and pale yellow-pink omental fat sit at the bottom of the field. No surgical clips, no cautery hooks, no smoke, and no active red bleeding are present.

Motion: slow, small, physically plausible movements only. The camera stays at the same distance and angle with very slight handheld drift. Instruments keep their exact shape, colour, size and entry side. Tissue moves only where an instrument touches it, deforms slightly and springs back.

Keep identical to the input image for the whole clip: the colours, the lighting, the image grain and sharpness, the circular endoscope vignette, and every anatomical structure not named above.

Strictly forbidden: new, extra, swapped or reshaped instruments; a new sac or organ appearing; smoke; zooms, camera cuts or jumps; text or overlays; changes of colour, exposure or image quality; human hands.
note: Control clip: two real frames of the same shot, the model fills the gap. Compared with the real footage between them. Never a training sample.
